Students will receive instruction from ATI instructors, who are experienced to teach a commercial driver course, through class time and driving time in order to help prepare them for the CDL test and will learn to be proficient at pre-trip and operational skills. Must have valid state issued driver?s license. Must hold a valid Ohio Commercial Learners Permit. Must pass Department of Transportation (DOT) Physical and Drug Test. A major must be declared, and the student must be full-time as part of a designated major. (These requirements are due to the institutions exemption status as a state-licensed school under exemption 4508.7, sections 4508.1 to 4508.6.
Prereq: Permission of instructor.

courses.description: Introduction to the science and business of chocolate. The course covers the history, agriculture and processing of cacao, components and nutritional benefits of chocolate, basic steps in the production of chocolate, uses of chocolate, marketing of chocolate and chocolate products, and current events related to chocolate agriculture, production, and marketing.

courses.subject: FDSCTE
courses.title: Wine and Beer in Western Culture
courses.description: To familiarize students with the terminology, production and practices related to wine, beer, and distilled spirits as well as critical historical and cultural events. Basic biology and chemistry understanding will help the student succeed.

courses.subject: FDSCTE
courses.title: Kitchen Science
courses.description: Students are introduced to sanitation rules, basic culinary/baking methods, fundamentals of cooking, & the science behind its methodology. Students gain an understanding of common foods & their function in cooking. Cooking techniques will be demonstrated & methodology for each formulation is explained on a scientific basis. Basic biology and chemistry understanding will help the student succeed.

courses.subject: FDSCTE
courses.title: Caffeine Science
courses.description: Explore the science of caffeine and production of caffeinated products, how it affects the human body along with a study of the historical importance of some of today's most popular caffeine sources.

courses.subject: FDSCTE
courses.title: The Science of Cooking
courses.description: This course covers the scientific method, sanitation, hygiene, and kitchen and laboratory safety; food components; weights and measurements; heat and heat transfer; cooking methods; food preservation; and tasting and evaluation of foods. Students taking the fully online course will need access to a stove and oven, refrigerator, and sink/faucet, and must provide their own equipment and ingredients.

Management aspects include site preparation, seasonality of management activities, and fundamentals of nutrient and pest management.

Prereq: GenMath 1040T or Math 1050 or math placement level R or higher.

Prereq: 2225T (EngTech 219T), 2230T (223T). Not open to students with credit for 225T.

courses.description:
Principles and practices of greenhouse bedding and flowering container plant production, including propagation, transplanting, nutrition, environmental requirements, height control, harvesting, pests, pathogens and post-harvest marketing.
Prereq: 2500T.

courses.subject: HORTTEC

courses.description:

Prereq: GenBiol 1250T or Biology 1113 or HCS 2202.
